claim: A screening-campaign/library axis dominates the naive Sanger organoid–cell-line comparison
citation: Dempster et al., Nature Communications (2019), Fig. 6 and Supplementary Data 1
specific_finding: Swapping library and assay duration in matched Broad/Sanger cell-line screens identified them as major drivers of the batch effect. Many biological dependencies were reproducible.
limit: The matched experiment used cell lines. No fraction of the Sanger organoid–line difference was identified as technical.

claim: A screening-campaign/library axis dominates the naive Sanger organoid–cell-line comparison
citation: Pacini et al., Nature Communications (2021)
specific_finding: Integrated independent Sanger and Broad cell-line screens using correction for experimental batch, guide efficiency and copy-number effects.
limit: Neither cohort was the 2026 Sanger organoid panel.

claim: A screening-campaign/library axis dominates the naive Sanger organoid–cell-line comparison
citation: Herranz-Ors et al., Nature (2026), Methods and Extended Data Fig. 8
specific_finding: Organoid library effects were corrected after retaining shared guides. Sixteen models were screened with both libraries. The authors also compared core fitness with cell lines.
limit: Correction within organoids does not calibrate the organoid campaign to Project Score. A joint technical-versus-biological variance decomposition was not reported.

claim: WRN MSI–MSS and KRAS mutant–wild-type CRISPR contrasts are each roughly halved in CRC organoids relative to Sanger CRC lines
citation: Herranz-Ors et al., Nature (2026), Fig. 4, Fig. 5a, Extended Data Fig. 9e
specific_finding: The release paper reported CRC organoid KRAS genotype/allele selectivity, WRN–MSI-linked features and four WRN-independent MSI organoids. It compared median fitness-gene counts across organoids and cell lines.
limit: Fitness-call counts and within-organoid effects are different estimands from two CRC within-platform contrast ratios. The publication uses the same underlying organoid resource.

claim: WRN MSI–MSS and KRAS mutant–wild-type CRISPR contrasts are each roughly halved in CRC organoids relative to Sanger CRC lines
citation: Gonçalves et al., Genome Biology (2021), Fig. 2 and Supplementary Fig. S7
specific_finding: The minimal library agreed with in-silico downsampling of organoid screens. In a paired HT-29 cell-line screen MinLibCas9 increased the dynamic range, including BRAF.
limit: Guide choice matters, but a smaller physical library alone need not compress scores. This comparison did not measure either CRC cohort ratio.

claim: WRN MSI–MSS and KRAS mutant–wild-type CRISPR contrasts are each roughly halved in CRC organoids relative to Sanger CRC lines
citation: Neiswender et al., Nature (2026), Fig. 2 and Extended Data Fig. 8
specific_finding: NextGen and traditional models showed shared KRAS-GOF addiction and selective differences in both directions. TP53-WT models had mean MDM2 scores of −0.54 vs −1.09.
limit: Different effects, lineages, scores and comparison groups. A pan-lineage mean is not a within-CRC genotype contrast. No joint Sanger WRN/KRAS half-ratio reported.

claim: WRN MSI–MSS and KRAS mutant–wild-type CRISPR contrasts are each roughly halved in CRC organoids relative to Sanger CRC lines
citation: Behan et al., Nature (2019), CRISPR–Cas9 screening Methods and Supplementary Table 1
specific_finding: The original Project Score CRISPR screens used KY/Yusa v1.0 and v1.1 at day 14, analyzing common guides. The authors reported MSI-selective WRN dependence in lines.
limit: No organoid-to-line effect-size ratio for both genes.

claim: Small BRAF V600E-selective knockout effect in CRC organoids relative to Sanger lines, attributed to EGF/EGFR bypass
citation: Prahallad et al., Nature (2012)
specific_finding: RAF inhibition rapidly activates EGFR feedback in BRAF V600E colon cancer cells. EGFR blockade potentiates the drug response.
limit: Drug-induced feedback in cell-line and in vivo models. Basal EGFR knockout and BRAF knockout with and without added EGF are different questions.

claim: Small BRAF V600E-selective knockout effect in CRC organoids relative to Sanger lines, attributed to EGF/EGFR bypass
citation: Ponsioen et al., Nature Cell Biology (2021), Figs 3–6
specific_finding: Single-cell ERK imaging in CRC organoids found EGFR amplification of oncogenic MAPK signaling. Long-term culture with reduced or absent EGF yielded heterogeneous ERK and inhibitor responses among BRAF V600E organoids.
limit: Direct medium manipulation with an ERK readout. No Sanger organoid/line BRAF knockout contrast.

claim: Small BRAF V600E-selective knockout effect in CRC organoids relative to Sanger lines, attributed to EGF/EGFR bypass
citation: Price et al., Scientific Reports (2022), Fig 5
specific_finding: In one Sanger BRAF V600E/MSI CRC organoid, BRAF knockout was in the top tenth of dependencies in both 5% and 80% extracellular matrix.
limit: Counterexample to uniformly weak dependency. One model, also named in the 2026 biobank code, cannot establish the population mean or isolate EGF.

claim: Small BRAF V600E-selective knockout effect in CRC organoids relative to Sanger lines, attributed to EGF/EGFR bypass
citation: El Bouazzaoui et al., iScience (2025), Fig 1
specific_finding: Isogenic correction of BRAF V600E in a CRC organoid restored dependence on EGF/EGFR signaling.
limit: Counterevidence to greater basal EGFR dependence in every V600E organoid. Isogenic correction differs from pooled BRAF knockout.

claim: Small BRAF V600E-selective knockout effect in CRC organoids relative to Sanger lines, attributed to EGF/EGFR bypass
citation: Kotarac et al., Journal of Experimental & Clinical Cancer Research (2026)
specific_finding: Ten BRAF V600E CRC organoids varied in sensitivity to combined BRAF and EGFR inhibition.
limit: Selected mutant pharmacology cohort. No genotype-stratified knockout ratio or attribution to medium.

claim: Small BRAF V600E-selective knockout effect in CRC organoids relative to Sanger lines, attributed to EGF/EGFR bypass
citation: Herranz-Ors et al., Nature (2026), Fig 5a–c
specific_finding: The release paper reports genotype-dependent KRAS/EGFR/PTPN11 effects and variable sensitivity to EGF withdrawal across KRAS alleles. BRAF alterations are annotated in Fig 5a.
limit: Same underlying screens. No reported BRAF organoid/line 0.16 ratio or controlled BRAF knockout by EGF interaction located.

claim: WRN dependency in MSI CRC organoids, including genetic and pharmacological evidence
citation: Chan et al., Nature (2019), Fig 2f,g
specific_finding: WRN shRNA impaired viability of a patient-derived MSI colon cancer organoid.
limit: Single-organoid validation alongside large cell-line screens.

claim: WRN dependency in MSI CRC organoids, including genetic and pharmacological evidence
citation: Picco et al., Cancer Discovery (2021)
specific_finding: Sanger-led genetic work directly shows WRN dependence in dMMR CRC organoids, including models derived from refractory disease.
limit: Pre-existing organoid genetic evidence. Cohorts include organoids as well as 2D lines, and counts across all models are not organoid counts.

claim: WRN dependency in MSI CRC organoids, including genetic and pharmacological evidence
citation: Price et al., Scientific Reports (2022), Fig 5
specific_finding: WRN knockout depleted the MSI CRC organoid in both tested matrix conditions.
limit: One model across two culture conditions. Related bioRxiv preprint posted 2021-10-24 (10.1101/2021.10.23.464385).

claim: WRN dependency in MSI CRC organoids, including genetic and pharmacological evidence
citation: Picco et al., Cancer Discovery (2024), Figs 3E and 4B–C
specific_finding: WRN inhibitors showed heterogeneous sensitivity in a cohort of 15 MSI and four MSS CRC organoids. Fourteen were CRISPR-screened. GSK_WRN3 activity tracked WRN knockout (published R² 0.705) and TA-repeat expansion.
limit: Both pharmacological and genetic evidence. HCMI models can overlap the release, and inhibition and knockout measure different effects.

claim: WRN dependency in MSI CRC organoids, including genetic and pharmacological evidence
citation: Khalili et al., Communications Biology (2025)
specific_finding: Independent Brunello knockout screening recovered the WRN synthetic lethal interaction in a mismatch repair-deficient colon cancer organoid.
limit: One parental genetic background with TP53 variants.

claim: WRN dependency in MSI CRC organoids, including genetic and pharmacological evidence
citation: Herranz-Ors et al., Nature (2026), Extended Data Fig 9e
specific_finding: Sanger reports WRN dependency and mismatch repair-associated features in CRC organoids. Four MSI organoids lacked WRN dependency and expanded TA repeats.
limit: Same biobank as #98. These cases limit claims of universal penetrance.

claim: WRN dependency in MSI CRC organoids, including genetic and pharmacological evidence
citation: Hao et al., Cancer Research (2026)
specific_finding: WRN inhibition enhanced anti-PD-1 effects in MSI CRC models including patient-derived tumor organoids.
limit: Immune-combination response is a distinct endpoint from basal WRN knockout dropout.
